---
title: "Lite vs full install"
---

ibleatools has two install variants. Picking the wrong one is either a missing-dependency
error or a very long install you did not need.

## Which do you need?

```bash
pip install -e .            # lite — the default
pip install -e ".[full]"    # full
```

| You want to | Install |
|---|---|
| Run a published model on existing features | lite |
| Compute `lf` / `csd` / `ap` features | lite |
| Aggregate and denoise features | lite |
| Download the IBL atlas aggregates | lite |
| Run the encoders and the probe transformer | lite |
| Compute `waveforms` (spike) features | **full** |
| Read NWB or SpikeInterface-Zarr recordings | **full** |
| Run the SDSC supercomputing pipeline | **full** |

If in doubt, start lite. It covers the whole
[tutorial](../tutorials/first-predictions.qmd) and every published model.

`pip install ibleatools[lite]` also works — `lite` is an explicit empty alias, so that
dependency line is valid, but it adds nothing over the base install. It exists because
[`ibl-alignment-gui`](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/ibl-alignment-gui) depends on
`ibleatools[lite]` and wanted to name its intent.

Both variants require **Python 3.12 or newer**. The floor was raised from 3.11 so the full
install resolves DARTsort ≥ 0.5.29 — the last DARTsort release supporting 3.11 is 0.5.28 —
and before that from 3.10 in version 0.7.0, because DARTsort 0.5 requires it.

## What lite includes

The base dependency set is deliberately substantial — lite is not a stub:

| package | for |
|---|---|
| `ibllib`, `ibl-neuropixel` ≥ 1.14 | ONE API, `ibldsp` destriping and waveform measures, `spikeglx` readers |
| `iblatlas` ≥ 1.2 | Brain regions, atlas volumes, genomics (the denoised MERFISH context) |
| `xgboost` | The region classifier |
| `torch` | The encoders and the probe transformer |
| `specparam` | Spectral-parameterisation features |
| `scikit-image` | Total-variation denoising |
| `scikit-learn` | Transformers and the feature pipeline |
| `pandera`, `pydantic` | Schema validation and typed parameters |
| `huggingface_hub` | Model download |
| `lfpack` ≥ 1.0 | Reading compressed LFP archives (release v04) |

Note that **torch is in the base install**. The torch models are a lite-install feature;
only the spike/waveform stack is gated.

## What full adds

| package | for |
|---|---|
| `dartsort` ≥ 0.5.25, `hdbscan`, `linear-operator`, `opt-einsum`, `h5py` ≥ 3.15.1 | Spike detection and waveform features |
| `spikeinterface` | The NWB and Zarr calculators |
| `pynwb`, `hdmf-zarr`, `remfile`, `fsspec`, `aiohttp`, `dandi` | Reading NWB, locally or streamed |
| `luigi`, `iblscripts` | The SDSC supercomputing pipeline |
| `ipykernel` | A Jupyter kernel for the environment |

## Why the split exists

Three reasons, in order of how much they matter.

**DARTsort is a heavy tree.** Spike detection needs `dartsort`, which pulls
`spikeinterface`, `hdbscan`, `linear-operator`, `dredge-ephys` and a recent `h5py`. Most
users of the region decoder never compute waveform features themselves — they consume
published features or compute the cheap LF families — and should not pay that install cost.

**Version floors are contagious.** The full extra needs `h5py>=3.15.1` to avoid a DARTsort
failure in the unit tests, and DARTsort's own floors move with each release (the reason
for the Python 3.12 floor above). Every such constraint narrows what else the environment
can hold, so confining them to an opt-in extra keeps the base install resolvable alongside
other packages.

**The GUI depends on lite.** `ibl-alignment-gui` requires ibleatools for model inference
and LF feature computation. Making the base install lite is what lets the GUI depend on it
without dragging in a spike-sorting stack.

## Lazy imports make the split work

The optional dependencies are imported **inside** the functions that need them, not at
module scope. So `import ephysatlas.feature_calculators` succeeds on a lite install even
though `NwbFeatureCalculator` cannot open a recording there — the failure arrives only when
you try to use it, and says exactly what to install:

```text
NWB feature computation needs the optional NWB/streaming dependencies
(spikeinterface, pynwb, hdmf-zarr, remfile, dandi).
Install them with `pip install ibleatools[full]`.
```

The same applies to `specparam` in `features.lf()`, `lfpack` in `read_lfp_features`, and
DARTsort in the spike path. It is why the docs CI can build the whole API reference from a
lite install.

## The xgboost / torch segfault

One import-order constraint is worth knowing about, because it shapes the code and can bite
you directly.

On macOS arm64, **xgboost and torch segfault when initialised together in the wrong
order.** `ephysatlas.regionclassifier` imports xgboost at module scope, so every
torch-using module in the package keeps `import torch` inside its methods rather than at
the top.

If you hit a `SEGFAULT` during feature computation, it is likely
[pytorch#132372](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/132372). Two workarounds — import
torch first, before anything else:

```python
import torch  # noqa: F401  — must come before the ephysatlas imports
```

or point the dynamic loader at your environment's torch libraries:

```bash
export DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=/path/to/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/lib
```

## Development installs

The repository uses [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) with three dependency groups:

```bash
uv sync                                  # lite
uv sync --extra full --group test        # what CI runs
uv sync --group docs                     # to build this site
uv sync --group lint                     # ruff
```

CI runs `uv sync --extra full --group test --group lint` on Python 3.12, then `ruff check`,
`ruff format --check` and the unittest suite with coverage.
